questions.question: What type of relationship is described between the exchange rate and the domestic interest rate?
questions.explanation: The speaker states that there is a positive relationship between the exchange rate and the domestic interest rate (Q0012, Q0014, Q0016).
questions.topic: exchange rate and interest rate relationship

original_segments.text: The equation tells me this has to happen
to exchange it, well, suppose that didn't happen to exchange it.
And then you say, oh, then I clearly invest in this bond.
This dominates the other one.
Well, that condition tells you, no, no.
In equilibrium, you have to be indifferent.
So the only thing that can move is exchange rate.
And exchange rate has to move until you're indifferent again
after you have done some argument
on the right-hand side.
That's the way you need to think about it.
So here, I'm just plotting this relationship
in the space of exchange rate in the x-axis
and the domestic interest rate here.
So that's an upward-sloping relation.
You can see here, as I move the interest rate up or the other
way around.
But anyways, if I move the interest rate up,
the exchange rate is going up.
So that's a positive relationship.
I can do it the other way around.
